He was selected as the 27th overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. Carroll played in the NBA for 11 seasons with the Grizzlies, [[Houston Rockets]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Utah Jazz]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Brooklyn Nets]] and [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]] and [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. ==Early life== Carroll was born to parents Ed, a pharmacist and minister, and Cynthia Carroll.{{cite web |last1=Birdsong |first1=Nick |title=Birmingham native, Atlanta Hawks star DeMarre Carroll's path to becoming an NBA starter has been anything but easy |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2015/02/post_647.html |website=AL.com |access-date=January 18, 2024 |date=February 12, 2015}} He was raised in [[Forestdale, Alabama]]. Carroll credits his inspiration to play basketball as his older brother DeLonte who died of a brain tumor at the age of nine. Carroll attended [[Minor High School]] in [[Adamsville, Alabama|Adamsville]] until he transferred to [[John Carroll Catholic High School (Birmingham, Alabama)|John Carroll Catholic High School]] in Birmingham prior to the start of the 2002–03 season. He partnered with Alabama [[point guard]] [[Ronald Steele]] at John Carroll Catholic to lead the Cavaliers to back-to-back Alabama Class 6A state titles.[http://www.ahsfhs.org/Basketball/champions.asp AHSAA Basketball Tournament Champions] He earned first team All-State, All-Area, All-Region, All-District and All-Metro recognition as a junior and senior and helped JCCHS to a combined 67–3 mark his final two seasons, culminating in those consecutive state crowns. He averaged 17.8 points and 9.1 rebounds as a junior for John Carroll's undefeated 36–0 state championship squad, before recording averages of 19.7 points and 10.7 rebounds as a senior en route to the team's 31–3 championship season. He capped his prep career by scoring a game-high 27 points in the annual Alabama-Mississippi All-Star Game and was named MVP of the 2004 Alabama Class 6A State Tournament. Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Carroll was listed as the No. 40 small forward and the No. 148 player in the nation in 2004.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-DeMarre-Carroll-15426;_ylt=AnDLmggsNX9RvSuVv3VyHXhGPZB4 DeMarre Carroll Recruiting Profile] ==College career== After a successful sophomore year at [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], he surprised the team when he decided to transfer to Missouri in 2006 to play for his uncle [[Mike Anderson (basketball, born 1959)|Mike Anderson]]. Carroll helped lead Missouri to the Elite Eight (national quarterfinals) of the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] during his senior year. He was nicknamed the "Junkyard Dog" because of his toughness and relentless play.[http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/carroll_demarre00.html DeMarre Carroll bio.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130517105623/http://www.mutigers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/carroll_demarre00.html |date=May 17, 2013 }} mutigers.com ===Health issues=== When Carroll came to Missouri, he complained of itchy legs, and was convinced that he was suffering from an [[allergy]]. After he was examined by several specialists, they came up with a considerably more serious diagnosis—[[liver]] disease. It was ultimately determined that Carroll would possibly need a [[Liver transplantation|liver transplant]], but not for at least 20 years after his diagnosis and most likely after the end of any potential professional basketball career. His illness was revealed several weeks before the [[2009 NBA draft]].{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/06/14/sports/ncaabasketball/14mizzou.html?_r=1 |title=Former Missouri Star Says Liver Disease Won't Stop Him |agency=Associated Press |newspaper=The New York Times |date=June 13, 2009 |access-date=August 31, 2009}} At 1:30 a.m. on July 5, 2007, Carroll was shot in the ankle during a domestic dispute at a nightclub in [[Columbia, Missouri]]. ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies (2009–2011)=== Carroll was drafted in the first round, 27th overall, by the Memphis Grizzlies.Tillery, Ronald (June 26, 2009). – "We got Thabeet – Griz believe UConn star will give them needed defensive spark". – ''[[The Commercial Appeal]]''. He played primarily off the bench during his tenure with the Memphis Grizzlies. On December 14, 2010, he was assigned to the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[NBA D-League]].[https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2010-12-14-3242975801_x.htm Grizzlies send Carroll to NBDL Dakota Wizards] He was recalled on January 5, 2011. ===Houston Rockets (2011)=== On February 24, 2011, Carroll was traded, along with [[Hasheem Thabeet]] and a future first-round draft pick, to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Shane Battier]] and [[Ish Smith]].[http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets_acquire_thabeet_dragi_2011_02_24.html Rockets Deal For Thabeet, Dragic And Carroll] On April 11, 2011, he was waived by the Rockets. ===Denver Nuggets (2011–2012)=== On December 12, 2011, the [[Denver Nuggets]] made Carroll a non-guaranteed training camp invitee. He appeared in four games with the Nuggets during the 2011–12 regular season before being waived on February 4, 2012.[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/218777/Nuggets_Waive_DeMarre_Carroll Nuggets Waive DeMarre Carroll] ===Utah Jazz (2012–2013)=== On February 8, 2012, Carroll signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].[http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/20120208_jazz_to_add_demarre_carroll.html Jazz Agrees to 1st Quarter.jpg|thumb|right|Carroll with the Brooklyn Nets in 2018]] On July 13, 2017, Carroll was traded, along with 2018 first and second round draft picks, to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Justin Hamilton (basketball, born 1990)|Justin Hamilton]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/07/13/brooklyn-nets-acquire-demarre-carroll-and-draft-picks-toronto|title=BROOKLYN NETS ACQUIRE DEMARRE CARROLL AND DRAFT PICKS FROM TORONTO|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2017|access-date=July 13, 2017}} In his debut for the Nets in their season opener on October 18, 2017, Carroll scored 10 points in a 140–131 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974701|title=Revamped Pacers rely on new faces to cut down Nets 140–131|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}} On November 26, 2017, he scored a season-high 24 points in a 98–88 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975040|title=Grizzlies bench Marc Gasol in fourth, extend skid to 8 losses|work=ESPN.com|date=November 26, 2017|access-date=November 26, 2017}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2019–2020)=== On July 6, 2019, Carroll was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in a three-team trade.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-acquire-demarre-carroll|title=SPURS ACQUIRE DEMARRE CARROLL|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2019}} ===Return to Houston (2020)=== After getting waived by the Spurs, Carroll was signed by the Houston Rockets on February 21, 2020.{{cite web |title=Rockets Sign Free Agent DeMarre Carroll |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-demarre-carroll |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 21, 2020 |date=February 21, 2020}} ==Coaching career== On August 2, 2022, Carroll was announced as an assistant coach for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He joined the staff of head coach [[Mike Budenholzer]] who Carroll played under on the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |title=Bucks Add DeMarre Carroll to Coaching Staff |url=https://www.nba.com/news/bucks-add-demarre-carroll-to-coaching-staff |website=NBA |access-date=November 10, 2022 |date=August 2, 2022}} On July 4, 2023, Carroll was hired as an assistant coach by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |title=Sources: Los Angeles Lakers hiring assistant coach DeMarre Carroll |url=https://www.espn.in/nba/story/_/id/37955586/los-angeles-lakers-hiring-assistant-coach-demarre-carroll?platform=amp |website=ESPN |access-date=August 26, 2023 |date=July 4, 2023}} On June 11, 2025, the [[Phoenix Suns]] hired Carroll to serve as an assistant coach under head coach [[Jordan Ott]].{{Cite web|title=Suns Hire 11-Year NBA Veteran to Coaching
